Services · CNC Machining

Custom PTFE Machining

CNC machined PTFE components made to your drawing, CAD file or sample — turned, milled, drilled and cut from virgin or filled PTFE, from a single prototype to repeat production.

Request a Quote WhatsApp

Many PTFE parts are too specific to buy off the shelf: a seat with an unusual profile, an insulator that has to fit an existing housing, a fixture for a laboratory rig. Our custom PTFE machining service turns PTFE stock into finished parts to your drawing, and because we also supply the rod, sheet and tube they are made from, grade and stock size can be chosen together.

What we machine

  • Turned and milled parts — plugs, nozzles, fittings, housings and manifolds.
  • Valve seats and stem packings — for ball, butterfly and plug valves in chemical service.
  • Electrical insulators — spacers, bushes and stand-offs, including insulators for aerospace and instrument assemblies.
  • Seals and bushes — non-standard seals and bushes machined to drawing.
  • Laboratory and semiconductor fixtures — carriers, holders and chemically inert parts for wet processing and lab equipment.
  • Food and pharma contact parts — scrapers, guides and fittings. Request compliance documentation for your requirement before ordering.
  • Prototypes — one-off and short-run parts to prove a design before production.

Machining processes

CNC turning

Round parts — rings, seats, bushes, plugs and threaded fittings — are turned from rod or tube. Turning suits most PTFE components, which are rotationally symmetric.

CNC milling

Pockets, slots, flats and non-round profiles are milled from sheet or block, for parts such as manifolds, carriers and insulating plates.

Drilling and tapping

Holes, cross-drillings and threads are added to turned or milled parts. Threads in PTFE are soft and can strip if over-tightened, so threaded inserts are worth considering for parts that will be assembled repeatedly.

Cutting

Rod is cut to length and sheet is cut into blanks, strips, rings and gaskets, either as finished parts or as blanks for further machining.

Why PTFE needs special handling

PTFE machines freely, but it does not behave like metal or even like most engineering plastics. Good parts depend on allowing for:

  • Creep (cold flow) — PTFE slowly deforms under sustained load, so fits and clamping forces relax over time.
  • High thermal expansion — roughly ten times that of steel, so heat from cutting or a change in room temperature moves the part.
  • The ~19 °C transition — PTFE has a crystalline transition near room temperature that causes a step change in dimensions. Measurements taken either side of it can differ, so critical dimensions need a stated measuring temperature.
  • Deformation under clamping — PTFE is soft, so heavy chuck or vice pressure distorts thin walls; the part springs back when released.
  • Burrs — PTFE tends to leave stringy burrs and feathered edges, which have to be removed without damaging sealing surfaces.

Sharp tools, light clamping and keeping heat down are the core of good PTFE machining. Our machining PTFE guide explains these effects in more detail.

Design tips for buyers

  • Apply tight tolerances only to the dimensions that need them — PTFE’s expansion makes tight tolerances everywhere costly and sometimes unachievable.
  • State the temperature at which critical dimensions are to be measured.
  • Avoid very thin walls and long, unsupported sections, which deflect during machining and in service.
  • Use filled grades for parts that carry load or wear; see virgin vs filled PTFE.
  • Consider whether PTFE is the right polymer at all — for high load and stiffness, compare PTFE vs PEEK.

How a custom order works

  1. Enquiry

    Send your drawing, CAD file or sample along with the quantity and application.

  2. Grade advice

    We review the duty and suggest virgin or a filled grade, and flag any features that are hard to hold in PTFE.

  3. Quotation

    We quote for material and machining, and confirm critical tolerances at this stage.

  4. Machining

    The parts are cut, turned, milled and drilled from suitable PTFE stock.

  5. Inspection

    Parts are checked against your drawing before they are packed.

  6. Dispatch

    Finished parts are packed and dispatched, with delivery across India and export enquiries welcome.

What to send for a quote

  • Drawing, CAD file or sample
  • Grade (or the operating conditions)
  • Quantity — prototype or batch
  • Critical dimensions and tolerances
  • Media, temperature and load

No drawing? A clear photo of a sample with key dimensions is often enough to start. Critical tolerances are confirmed at quotation.
